# `formal/vendor` — the implementers' models, vendored

The models the implementing repositories keep of their own parts, copied here so that this repository's end-to-end account can name them by bytes and commit. [`VENDOR.tsv`](VENDOR.tsv) lists every vendored file in this directory, in `formal/onion_layers/` and in `formal/cewp_node/catalog/`. For each one it gives the repository, ref and commit it came from, its path there, the sha256 of the upstream bytes, and the sha256 of the bytes here. Where the two differ, the `note` says why (in every case so far, CC section numbers re-cut to this edition's, or comment wording).

| Directory | From | What it models | Where the path from screen to packet uses it |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`client/csd5`](client/csd5/) | CIRISClient `main` | one TLA+ module per CSD/5 card, generated by the client's checker: a screen's states and the exits from each | the screen: what a person may do at each state |
| [`agent/h3ere_ctxflow`](agent/h3ere_ctxflow/) | CIRISAgent `main` (merged as #1367) | what each stage of one agent thought receives, the contract that fixes where context is lost, and a check of contract against measured | the agent: from what it is shown to the act it proposes |
| [`server/add_device`](server/add_device/) | CIRISServer `main` | a new device joining its owner's identity, under careless, live, safety and Sybil configurations | the key plane: a person's second device |
| [`kernel`](kernel/) | CIRISKernel `main` (7f4fb7cbcae5) | four proofs of rules of this text: the three admissions as one walk (`Admission.lean`, 76 theorems, with the two ways an act has its authority), the age rules in any order of arrival: the void rule for a minor's duty appointment (`MinorVoid.tla`, `MinorVoid.lean`), the band at an act's instant (`MinorSuspend.tla`) and the standing protections on the rows held (`StandingProtection.tla`), each with its configurations and plants, that a statement's key is a key of its issuer (`KeyOfIssuer.lean`, 44 theorems), that derived content reaches only those who may see every piece it drew on (`DerivedCircle.lean`, 12 theorems), and the end of a standing read from what rows name, with no instant: what counted, what stays in force, who may receipt and what a count may lift (`ConferralEnd.tla` with its configurations and plants, its verdict `CONFERRAL_END.md`, the reading of this text against it `CONFERRAL_END_TEXT_CHECK.md`, its reference `conferral_end.py` with the fixture `conferral_end.json` and `.tsv`, and the cross-check of reference against spec `conferral_xcheck.py`), with the rule for a room's content after a member's seat ends (section I of the verdict: the reference `conferral_content.py`, its exhaustive run `check_conferral_content.py` and the fixture `conferral_content.json`; a run, not a TLC result), and the row that needs two standings (section J of the verdict: its exhaustive run `check_conferral_two.py` and the fixture `conferral_two.json`; a run, not a TLC result), all at `65bf508df73a`; the crate that computes these rules is `kernel-v0.2.2` (`08028c41a1c7`, modules `conferral`, `content` and `derived`) | admission, the age rules, the verification order and the end of a standing ([CC 2.4.1.1](../../constitution/part_2_the_grammar.md#2.4.1.1)): proved or checked over every row set, not only the cases run here |
| [`edge`](edge/) | CIRISEdge `main` | the transport tiers, rooms over the onion, the event path, the reply lane, the retry schedule (quantitative) | transport: load and capacity, not security |
| [`../onion_layers`](../onion_layers/) | CIRISEdge `feat/onion-fsd` | the anonymous tier's layer deal (TLA+ and Lean) | transport: the onion tier |
| [`../cewp_node/catalog`](../cewp_node/catalog/) | CIRISServer `main` | the twenty topologies the harness stands up on real nodes | the node as a whole |
| *pinned, not copied* ([`PINS.tsv`](PINS.tsv)) | CEWP `main` | the network simulation (the twin, calibrated from the live mesh), its specs, and the kernel compiled to WASM that the mesh page folds every node with | the whole path at scale: rows moving between devices, each folding with the kernel |

The CEWP twin is too large to copy, so it is cited by commit: `PINS.tsv` gives the repository, ref, commit, path and git tree id of each piece.

**Checked.** `python3 tools/vendor_models.py --check` (CI) holds every listed file to its recorded hash, refuses a file under a vendored directory that the manifest does not list, and refuses an edit made here without a note. `--upstream`, run where the repositories are cloned, re-hashes each file at its recorded commit and names the files whose ref has moved on since. After a re-vendor, `--write` re-hashes the local copies.

**Running them.** These models run in their own repositories' CI. They are vendored so they can be cited and diffed here, not re-run. The models this repository runs itself are listed in [`../README.md`](../README.md).
